newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 96/97 budget deficit seen at 63.2 billion baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai 96/97 budget deficit seen at 63.2 billion baht.

text.p: The Thai government will end the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) fiscal year with an estimated 63.2 billion baht ($2.43 billion) budget deficit, its first deficit in a decade, the Budget Bureau said on Wednesday.
The bureau said in a paper presented to the cabinet that total government expenditures this year would amount to about 944 billion baht against 880.84 billion in revenue.

But Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told reporters the government's actual operating budget this year will carry a smaller cash deficit of slightly more than 20 billion bhat as part of the shortfall would be covered by non-tax revenue.
Thailand's sharply-slowing economy, projected to grow by about five to six percent this year, has prevented the govenrment from meeting its original tax revenue target.

Thailand's original 1996/97 tax revenue target was 984 billion baht. The adjustment on Wednesday was the second time the government has lowered the figure. In January it reduced the target to 925 billion baht.

The 63.2 billion baht budget deficit is expected despite a 59 billion baht spending cut already announced by the government in its effort to sustain a balanced, deficit-free budget. It has posted balanced budgets for the past nine years.
